answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by growing trust on a trellis instead of handing it out freely. A newcomer starts as a faint point in a nebula of unproven identities and must complete a verifiable service task that no script can fake at scale. Two unrelated established agents co-sign the result, staking a small bond on it, and the newcomer's standing climbs like a vine along the trellis only as independent peers confirm further real work. If fraud is found, the whole branch is cut and the sponsors lose their bonds, so faking many identities costs more than it can ever earn.
